name: Linz oxygen-blowing trials
summary: In 1949 converter trials at Linz found that gentler oxygen blowing from a lance held further away gave steel good enough to roll into sheet.
description: Lower oxygen pressure and a more distant lance yielded steel suitable for rolling into sheet in converter trials.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.

date.basis: VÖEST chronology: trials began 3 June; changed lance position and pressure on 25 June; larger experimental vessel in October.

date.basis: The U.S. District Court’s decision is dated 6 July 1966; the exact date of Federal Supplement publication has not been established.

events.statement: In its patent decision, the district court described the 1949 Linz trial sequence and treated the reduced-pressure, higher-lance results as a satisfactory oxygen-blowing process.
events.population: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan and the parties to the patent case
events.caveats: This is legal recognition of reported historical trial results, not independent metallurgical validation or adoption of the 1949 pilot apparatus. Federal Supplement publication date and earlier technical-publication history remain unverified.
